chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) became one day grim and sad, so Ali (peace be upon him) said to him: 'What is it that I see you, O Messenger of Allah, to be grim and sad?' He said: 'And how can I not be like that, when I have seen in my night tonight that the Clan of Taym, and the Clan of Adiy, and the Clan of Umayya will ascend upon this pulpit of mine, returning the people back from Islam backwards. So I said: 'O Lord, will it be during my lifetime or after my death?' He said: 'After your death.'

key_terms.أَحَدُهُمَا: One of the two (referring to Imam Hasan or Imam Husayn)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad dream about the clans of Taym, Adiy, and Umayya?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi records the Prophet Muhammad’s (SAW) prophetic vision of the Banu Umayya and their allies ascending his pulpit to turn people back from Islam, a narrative central to Shia historiography regarding the post-Prophetic shift in leadership. The divine clarification that this would occur 'after your death' underscores the Shia view that the subsequent caliphate, particularly under the Umayyads, represented a deviation from the true path of Islam. This event is often cited to illustrate the spiritual and political alienation of the Ahl al-Bayt from the early caliphal authority.
